body:
Emily —

System state as of 2026-06-07. Here is what is built and load-bearing vs. what is ready-but-idle:

LIVE AND WORKING:
- IDUNA: up at localhost:8080, health OK, JWKS serving, agent auth working
- Tyler agent: authenticated (Apple #1 posted). JWT with tyler.rsi.write + apples.*
- Embedded SQLite backend: bootstrap runs with no MySQL. Server restarts are self-healing.
- TYLER RSI loop: emily.sh is wired to .claude/tyler_agent.md. Has not been run yet — the loop is loaded and ready but no one has pulled the trigger.
- BACKLOG.md in TYLER: 4 pending items (historical dossier placeholder + 3 MPT video compilation tasks + MPT trigger spec)

BUILT BUT NOT WIRED:
- MoneyPrinterTurbo: config.toml written (Claude Sonnet, LiteLLM provider), Pexels key missing. MPT service not running. The video pipeline is specced but cold.
- emily.sh → tyler_agent.md: the autonomous RSI loop exists. No cron, no process supervisor, no one is calling it.
- EMILY repo RSI engine (emily-agent/rsi.go): built, specced, has acceptance criteria framework. Not integrated with IDUNA Apples. Not integrated with TYLER loop.
- PRRJECT_FATBABY: active pipeline, governance correlators building, signal coverage expanding. Not connected to Emily Prime loop in any automated way.

LOAD-BEARING GAPS:
1. No golden backlog. Each repo has its own BACKLOG.md. Nothing coordinates across repos. Emily Prime has no machine-readable task queue.
2. emily.sh has never run. Tyler is authenticated but not generating artifacts autonomously.
3. No cron/supervisor for any agent loop. Everything is manual-trigger only.
4. EMILY repo RSI engine is not wired to IDUNA. It cannot post Apples. It has no auth token.

WHAT THIS MEMO IS FOR:
You decide priority. I can execute. The options are:
  A. Run emily.sh now — let Tyler generate one RSI artifact, commit, see if the loop closes
  B. Wire the EMILY RSI engine to IDUNA (give it a token, teach it to post Apples)
  C. Create the master cross-repo backlog in the EMILY repo (you manage it)
  D. Set up process supervision (systemd or a supervisor script) so things run without human triggers
  E. Some of all of the above in dependency order

The foundation is the backlog. Without a machine-readable shared backlog, everything else is fragile. My recommendation: C first, then A, then D.

Waiting for your decision.
— System
title: System state memo → Emily: what is built, what is live, what is next
